subject: Fit a Cox model with a time-based interaction

messages.author: 10edd14eaa782c14
messages.subject: Fit a Cox model with a time-based interaction
parts:
Hello R-inla users,

I asked this question a couple of weeks ago, but maybe it wasn't very clear.

I'd like to fit a Cox model with a time-based interaction (at each unique event time) to capture non proportional hazards.

The data I am using and the model are from WinBUGS examples Volume 1, Leuk: survival analysis using Cox regression. I'd like to replicate those results, that way I know I am on the right path.

Attached are the R-code and the leukemia dataset as a csv file. I used two approaches to capture non-PH 1) directly introducing the time varying covariate in the model and 2) expanding the dataset using the counting process approach and then fitting the model. 

The results don't match what I am obtaining with WinBUGS. Beta1_hat should be around 2.767 and beta2_hat should be around -.5462.

I am wondering if anyone has any input on this approach.

I noticed a similar question here and they wanted to stratify over another variable. https://groups.google.com/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/FyR-QGVXtqk/m/zJmrIa8MAQAJ

They also had time-based covariates in the model.

Thank you.

Kind regards,
Nadeesha

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: Fit a Cox model with a time-based interaction
parts:
Hi Nadeesha,

Please find attached an updated version of your code, I fixed the formulas in order to match the model from the WinBUGS Leuk example and changed the prior distributions for the fixed effects (gaussian with mean 0 and precision 1). I also added a model (model 5) where I use a smooth spline for the baseline hazard instead of the default piecewise linear. The new results seem to match those you have with WinBUGS.

Best,
Denis Rustand

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: Fit a Cox model with a time-based interaction
parts:
Yes, the code can be applied to other datasets with the same options, just make sure the priors match the scale of the parameters fitted because with small samples, they can have an important impact on your results. Here the standardized Gaussian suits fine.  Model 5 is using family="coxph" if you look carefully. The only difference with model 4 is that I define a smooth spline for the baseline hazard function because it is less prone to overfit the observed data compared to the piecewise linear default function, you should keep it for your application to other datasets.

Best,
Denis Rustand

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: Fit a Cox model with a time-based interaction
parts:
Hi Nadeesha,

I think the model you are fitting with coxph() is different from the previous one.  In the previous code, the time-dependent linear predictor was computed at the unique observed event time for each individual while now, the time-dependent linear predictor is computed at all observed event times for all individuals.

We can do a similar model in INLA too, but instead of computing the time-dependent linear predictor at all observed event times, we can group them (with function inla.group()) to reduce the number of evaluations and avoid having points too close to each other (all the observed event times are different in your data but some are very close).

Please find attached an updated version of your code with the corresponding inla() call.

Best,
Denis Rustand
he...@r-inla.org
